header.running_head: The Abstinence of Hadhrat Mus'ab Bin Umayr (RA)

blocks.text: His Statement about How Much of Public Funds are Permissible for the Khalifah

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Razeen reports that they once went to meet Hadhrat Ali (RA) on the occasion of Eidul Adha. Hadhrat Ali (RA) served them a dish prepared with cubes of meat and bran. We remarked, "May Allaah always keep you well! It would have been better if you had fed us duck because Allaah has given plenty." Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, "O Ibn Razeen! I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'It is not permissible for a Khalifah to take anything from Allaah's money (public funds) besides two dishes. One for himself and his family and the other to place before people.'"[^1]
The Abstinence of Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA)

Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once went to see Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA), he found him lying down on a saddle blanket, using the animal's satchel as a pillow. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Why have you not adopted that (luxuries) which your companions have adopted?" Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) replied, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! This is sufficient to take me to the grave." In his narration, Hadhrat Ma'mar narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) arrived in Shaam, the common people as well as the leaders came to meet him. "Where is my brother?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked. "Who is he?" the people enquired. "Abu Ubaydah," Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied. The people said, "Here he comes." When Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) came, Hadhrat Umar (RA) descended from his animal and embraced him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then went to Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA)'s house and saw nothing there but his sword, his shield and his conveyance. The rest of the narration is similar to the one above.[^2]
The Abstinence of Hadhrat Mus'ab Bin Umayr (RA)
The Narration of Hadhrat Ali (RA) and the Statement of Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Ali (RA) says, "One winter morning I left home extremely hungry with the cold almost killing me. There was a piece of undyed leather at home which was still smelly. I cut it to put my head through and tied it to my chest to ward off the cold.
